name: Boeing B-29 Superfortress
blurb: A four-engine pressurized heavy bomber with retractable tricycle gear and eight 1,000 lb bombs carried inside the hull. Its speed, climb and stall figures are the Army's printed 1944 estimates, not flight-test data; a failed engine, the bomb-bay doors and the remote turrets are not modeled.
history:
The Boeing B-29 Superfortress was a four-engined heavy bomber designed for high-altitude strategic bombing, with a pressurized cabin, tricycle landing gear and a computer-controlled system that let gunners aim four remote turrets. It was one of the largest aircraft of the war, and its design and production cost more than the Manhattan Project.

Against Japan it flew high-altitude raids, low-level night incendiary raids and mining missions to blockade Japanese waters. B-29s dropped the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. 3,970 were built.

In this game the B-29 flies to the numbers printed in the Army Air Forces' 1944 pilot's manual for the airplane: about 323 mph at 20,000 feet and 850 feet a minute at sea level, at 110,000 pounds. Those charts are estimates, and no flown test report was found, so the flight model is fitted to them and its take-off run reads about 29 percent longer than the chart's 2,725 feet. The four engines are modeled as one engine with their summed power, and all four propellers turn; if one fails the game does not notice. The bomb bays are drawn without doors, so the eight bombs, 8,000 pounds in all, drop straight through the belly; the airplane could carry up to 20,000 pounds, but the game allows eight racks and reuses the 1,000 lb bomb. The five remote turrets and their guns are drawn but do not move or fire. The drawn landing gear stands about 6 feet taller than the real airplane's.

sources.title: B-29 Pilot's Flight Operating Instructions, AN 01-20EJ-1 (estimates as of 1 Jul 1944); a scan found by web search, no stable URL recorded, so the link is the article read alongside it
